**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The agreement imposes no non-solicitation, no-hire, or employee-inducement restriction on our side (Issuer/Depositor) or on anyone. This matches the playbook's **preferred** position — "No non-solicit on Customer" — so nothing needs to change.

What I checked:
- Full-text searches for "solicit", "hire", "induce", "personnel" — no hits at all.
- "employ" hits are unrelated: no-recourse-against-personnel provisions (p0244, p0284), the "Indemnified Person" definition (p0291), and ERISA/Benefit Plan definitions (p0649, p0651, p0740, p0770).
- Article IX ("Other Agreements", the most likely home for a stray restrictive covenant) — contains only financing statements, no transfer/lien, expenses, receivables information, no petition, limited recourse, limitation of liability, tax treatment, Regulation RR risk retention, and the Cap Collateral Account. No restrictive covenants on personnel.
- Article VII successor servicer / transition-of-servicing provisions — impose cooperation and remittance duties on Cellco, but no restriction on the Issuer, Depositor, or a Successor Servicer hiring Cellco's servicing staff.

Note for the file: this is consistent with the deal type — an employee non-solicit is unusual in a securitization transfer and servicing agreement. Worth flagging commercially that the absence of any hiring restriction is favorable to us, since a Successor Servicer may need to recruit experienced servicing personnel on a transition; we should resist any attempt to add one on a later turn.
